subject: Deployment gating: EU & APAC private deployment - data plane cutover pre-checks
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Marco Silva <marco@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 08:12:00 +0000
Subject: Deployment gating: EU & APAC private deployment - data plane cutover pre-checks

Marco / ACME ops team —

Thanks again for working with us on the private deployment cutover window next week. Attached is a concise pre-checklist we plan to use at T-48 / T-2 hours. High-level asks before we lock the window: 

- Confirm IP ranges for the EU and APAC VPC peering (we need the exact prefixes for routing ACLs).
- Confirm sidecar egress policy will allow outbound KMS/HSM calls to the key proxy in the EU anchor region.
- Provide the ASN and BGP communities ACME will apply for emergency route withdrawal testing.
- Verify MTU across the transit path (we occasionally see fragmentation > 1400 bytes).

Notes: we plan a staged data-plane cutover with a single-customer canary in APAC for 30 minutes before scaling to 10% traffic, then EU canaries shortly after. Our canary runbook is attached; the ops rollback trigger is strictly timeboxed (15 minutes) + error rate thresholds.

Attachments: cutover-prechecks.pdf, network-diagram-v2.png

Please respond with the confirmations you can provide today and any outstanding blocking items. If you prefer a quick 20-minute call this afternoon (UTC) we can walk the checklist.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Sr. Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0142
From: Marco Silva <marco@acmecloud.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:07:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Deployment gating: EU & APAC private deployment - data plane cutover pre-checks

Stephanie —

Thanks for the checklist, looks good. Quick answers below and a couple follow-ups: 

- EU prefixes: 10.44.0.0/16 (control), 10.45.0.0/16 (data). APAC prefixes: 10.54.0.0/16 (control), 10.55.0.0/16 (data). We'll attach a signed CIDR allocation PDF to the final cutover notice.
- KMS calls: confirmed. The proxy accepts requests only from our peered VPC subnets; we will add the Redwood data-plane IPs to allowlist.
- ASN: AS64512. We will honor community 64512:666 for immediate withdraw during rollback drills.
- MTU: we are on 1500 end-to-end for the transit path shown in your diagram. We will run a traceroute + jumbo test before T-48.

Outstanding: we need to validate your canary session sticky hashing for signed tokens in APAC. If the session affinity persists on failover, it could surface a small user impact spike (non-persistent, but visible). Can you confirm if the canary will force token revalidation after cutover?

I'll join a call at 14:00 UTC if that works for your team.

—Marco
Marco Silva
Platform Ops Lead, ACME Cloud Solutions
marco@acmecloud.com
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marco Silva <marco@acmecloud.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 11:25:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Deployment gating: EU & APAC private deployment - data plane cutover pre-checks

Stephanie / team —

Summary of internal adjustments based on Marco's note and our internal run-through: 

1) Token revalidation: we will enable a short TTL (30s) for canary sessions in APAC and force a re-issue on the first request after the cutover event. That ensures affinity doesn't mask misrouting. QA already validated token re-issue flow; I flagged a minor client retry behavior that we covered in the canary-runbook.md (attached).

2) Canary plan (concise):
  - T0: route 0.5% traffic for 30 mins to canary hosts (APAC). Metric watch: latency P95, 5xx rate, packet drop.
  - Escalation/rollback: if 5xx > 1.5% or P95 > baseline + 75ms for 2 consecutive 5-min windows, rollback to pre-cutover routing which withdraws BGP community 64512:666.
  - If canary passes, expand to 10% for 1 hour, then to 50% with the EU canary mirroring 10% cadence.

3) Network ops asks for staging: ACME to publish BGP test session at T-24 and an emergency withdraw test at T-2 (synthetic for us to validate failback).

4) Compliance & logs: we will attach a short proof bundle with control-plane audit entries and KV cache stubs for the canary window for ACME legal / security. Expect a shared Drive link post-run.

5) SLA exception: this cutover needs a 2-hour warm window where latency SLOs are relaxed for impacted tenants to avoid false-positive alerting. I request Lauren's sign-off to proceed with the exception and to inform CS/Oncall.

I've attached the canary-runbook.md and added the INFRA ticket (https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INFRA-9421). If Marco can confirm the session-sticky detail and the planned T-2 withdraw test, we can lock the slot.

-Vivek
Head of Deployment Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Deployment gating: EU & APAC private deployment - data plane cutover pre-checks

Team —

Thanks — reviewed and authorized. Approved: 2-hour warm window SLA exception, proceed with the staged canary plan as documented. Please ensure CS and Oncall receive the timing notice and the short proof bundle after the canary completes. Procurement/Reserved capacity teams: schedule the Dedicated capacity reservation for the cutover date under deal DL-ACME-202611 and confirm billing contact.

Marco — thanks for the network confirmations; please post the T-2 withdraw test time to this thread when available.

Approved,
Lauren Bishop
VP, Customer Operations & Delivery
Redwood Inference
